text.p: Grand Casinos Inc said Tuesday that the U.S. District Court for the District of Nevada has dismissed a lawsuit brought by Stratosphere Corp shareholders against Stratosphere, Grand Casinos and some of the officers of both companies.
The allegations made in suit included claims that Grand Casinos, Stratosphere, and some of their officers and directors violated certain securities laws and regulations.
Grand Casinos owns 42 percent of the stock of Stratosphere.

The court found that the shareholders failed to specifically allege facts constituting fraud in connection with a prospectus issued by Stratosphere and in public statements and filings, Grand Casinos said in a statement.

In February, some defendants including Grand Casinos submitted motions to dismiss. In an order entered May 21, the court dismissed the lawsuit with respect to all claims and all defendants, finding the plaintiffs failed to state a claim, Grand Casinos said.
Grand Casinos remains a defendant in a pending litigation in Nevada state court brought by Stratosphere shareholders against various defendants including Grand Casinos.
The state litigation is based on claims similar to those in the federal lawsuit which was dismissed.
Grand Casinos owns and operates three casino hotel resorts in Mississippi, manages two land- based casinos in Louisiana, and manages two casino hotel resorts in Minnesota.
